RESOLVE App

Source: vignettes/articles/app.Rmd
app.Rmd

Predict a vegetation plot’s EUNIS habitat, altitude, slope, plot area, survey year and location from the species recorded on it, with the released models trained on the European Vegetation Archive’s plots. The models run in your browser: your files are read inside this tab and are not uploaded anywhere. The page downloads the models and the elevation model from Zenodo (models, elevation model), the map from OpenStreetMap and, for a map download, the country boundaries from Eurostat GISCO.

Habitats

    Predictions

          Each variable is predicted by five models, trained in the same way from different random starting points (seeds), and the page combines their five predictions: habitat by majority vote (seed agreement is the share of the five naming the habitat), numeric variables by their mean and standard deviation, and location by the spherical mean and the median distance of the five from it.

          Altitude and slope can also be corrected with an elevation model (Copernicus GLO-30). The correction weighs the prediction against the elevation model's value at the plot and over the square kilometre around it, depending on the plot's location uncertainty, the spread of the five predictions and how many of the plot's species the models know. The table gives the elevation model's own values beside the corrected ones.
